Chapter 6 Practice

Checkpoint 1–3

Answers to the three sets of checkpoint questions in the Chapter 6 slides. The pages on this site also demonstrate the HTML and CSS ideas.

Checkpoint 1 — Box model and CSS positioning

  1. List the parts of the box model.

    From the inside out: content, padding, border, and margin.

  2. What is the difference between relative and absolute positioning?

    Relative positioning moves an element from where it would normally be. Absolute positioning places an element at a specific spot based on its nearest positioned container (or the page if there is none).

  3. What does the float property do?

    The float property moves an element to the left or right so other content can wrap around it.

Box model example: This box has content, padding, a border, and margin around it.

Checkpoint 2 — Layout and CSS tools

  1. Resize the practice page. What happens, and what layout is used?

    On my demonstration practice page, the content grows and shrinks with the browser up to a maximum width. This is a jello layout because it is flexible on smaller screens but stops growing past a set size.

    The original chapter6/practice/index.html from Hands-On Practice 6.5 was not included with the provided files, so this answer describes the demo page supplied here instead.

  2. Name a helpful CSS debugging tip.

    I find it helpful to check the CSS for missing semicolons or brackets, then use the W3C CSS Validator if I cannot spot the problem.

  3. When should you use an element selector, class, or id?

    Use an element selector for all tags of that type, a class for styles that can be reused, and an id for one specific element on the page.

Checkpoint 3 — HTML5 structural elements

  1. Why use structural HTML5 elements instead of divs?

    Elements like header, nav, main, article, and footer make it easier to tell what each part of the page is for.

  2. What is the purpose of article?

    The article element holds content that could stand on its own, like a news story or blog post.

  3. What is the purpose of hgroup?

    The hgroup element groups a heading with related heading text, such as a title and subtitle.
